cards.text: Psalm 120 starts with a label: "A song of ascents." The writer looks back on a time of distress. And in that distress, the writer cried out to the LORD.

cards.question: When the writer cried out to the LORD in distress, the LORD answered.

cards.text: Then the psalm prays: "Deliver my soul, O LORD…" And it names exactly what the trouble is.

cards.question: The writer prays, "Deliver my soul, O LORD…" Deliver from what?

answers.text: Lying lips and a deceitful tongue
A strong enemy and a mighty army
Hunger and a dry and weary land

cards.text: Then the song turns and talks right to that deceitful tongue: "What will He do to you…" And the next line? A warrior shows up.

cards.question: Right after the question to the deceitful tongue, a warrior shows up. What comes from the warrior?

cards.text: Sharp arrows from the warrior, with burning coals of the broom tree! Then the writer talks about home: Meshech, a nation, and the tents of Kedar, a desert tribe.

cards.question: The writer is happy to be living in Meshech and among the tents of Kedar.
It's not just where the writer lives. It's who. The writer says the people there ___ peace.
The writer says living among people who hate peace has only gone on for a short while.

cards.text: Last line of the song, friend, and the writer says, "I am in favor of peace…" Me too, baker, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer refereeing the dead batteries over who had the most charge left.

cards.question: The writer is in favor of peace. But when the writer speaks, the people there want ___.
